Application examples

Choose a complete example window, select your addon’s language, and download its source file. Each example includes its controls, drawing, input, and cleanup. Start with the settings window for Apply and Cancel, or use the file browser when work must load in the background.

Use an example

Choose a language, download its single source file, and add it to your Minecraft 1.12.2 Cleanroom addon. Each file contains the complete window behavior, drawing, input handling and cleanup. Java, Kotlin, Scala and Groovy call the shared screen API directly. Only ZenScript requires CraftTweaker; it uses the registered script names. All variants require OffscreenCleanroom. Enable the chosen JVM language in your addon build; the server example also requires ModularUI.

Call open() from a client key or button handler after joining a world. Call close() from your client disconnect or unload hook. Declaring the callbacks opens nothing. The server-action file additionally provides register() for common initialization on both sides; the ZenScript file calls it during script loading.

The library connects each screen to native-window drawing and input through its vanilla adapter. Local drawing, input and update callbacks run on the client thread. A returned handle owns a window but may precede its first layout; isReady() (or ready in ZenScript) reports readiness. Each file closes only its own handles. Server action callbacks run on the server thread and must finish using their borrowed context before returning.

Settings: Apply, Cancel and Reset

Edit a private draft, reject an empty name, restore defaults without saving, and apply changes to a UTF-8 text file. Cancel discards the draft. Reopen the window to load the saved value. This small local-file example writes on the client thread; use a worker for large or remote configuration files.

package examples.single.java;

// Requires OffscreenCleanroom on Minecraft 1.12.2 Cleanroom.
// Add this file to your addon with its language runtime enabled.
// Call open() from a client key/button handler after joining a world; declarations open nothing.
// Call close() from your client-thread disconnect/unload hook.
// The server-action example additionally registers its panel during common startup on both sides.
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.script.OffscreenWindows;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.script.OffscreenWindows.*;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.script.OffscreenFiles;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.script.OffscreenFiles.*;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.script.OffscreenPanel;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.script.OffscreenPanel.Context;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.script.OffscreenPanel.Player;

public final class SettingsExample {
    // Retain the exact native handle. A title is not unique enough to prove ownership.
    private static Window owned = null;
    // Draw the same compact header at the current GUI size. Rendering stays on the client thread.
    public static void header(ScreenEvent event) {
        event.rect(0, 0, event.getWidth(), event.getHeight(), -15722464);
        event.rect(20, 20, 3, 16, -10103043);
        event.text("Settings", 32, 23, -1445387, false);
        event.text("Edit a draft, then apply it to disk.", 32, 42, -6372673, false);
        event.rect(20, 62, event.getWidth() - 40, 1, -13614255);
    }
    
    // Small local arithmetic helper; it is included rather than supplied by a hidden utility file.
    public static int minInt(int a, int b) {
        if (a < b) {
            return a;
        }
        return b;
    }
    
    // Clamp layout and scrolling without allocating objects during drawing.
    public static int maxInt(int a, int b) {
        if (a > b) {
            return a;
        }
        return b;
    }
    
    // Build fresh screen state, declare callbacks, then open once. A returned handle can precede
    // the first layout; readiness is separate from ownership. No window opens during file loading.
    public static void open() {
        close();
        Screen screen = OffscreenWindows.screen("Settings", 960, 640);
        TextResult loaded = OffscreenFiles.read("config/offscreen-settings.txt",
            "Player");
        screen.textField("name", 36, 105, 400, 24, loaded.value()).maxLength(40);
        screen.getDefaults().text("message", "Edit the name, then apply your changes.");
        if (!loaded.success()) {
            screen.getDefaults().text("message", loaded.error());
        }
        screen.button("Apply changes",
            36,
            158,
            120,
            26,
            clicked -> apply(clicked))
            .flat()
            .shadow(false)
            .skin("normal",
            -15062988,
            -13614255,
            -1445387,
            1)
            .skin("hovered",
            -13612969,
            -10037571,
            -1445387,
            1);
        screen.button("Cancel",
            168,
            158,
            100,
            26,
            clicked -> cancel(clicked))
            .flat()
            .shadow(false)
            .skin("normal",
            -15062988,
            -13614255,
            -1445387,
            1)
            .skin("hovered",
            -13612969,
            -10037571,
            -1445387,
            1);
        screen.button("Reset",
            280,
            158,
            100,
            26,
            clicked -> reset(clicked))
            .flat()
            .shadow(false)
            .skin("normal",
            -15062988,
            -13614255,
            -1445387,
            1)
            .skin("hovered",
            -13612969,
            -10037571,
            -1445387,
            1);
        screen.on("draw", event -> draw(event));
        owned = screen.open();
    }
    
    // The widget renders its own editable field; this callback draws labels and validation feedback.
    public static boolean draw(ScreenEvent event) {
        header(event);
        event.text("DISPLAY NAME", 36, 85, -6372673, false);
        event.text(event.getState().text("message"), 24, 215, -1445387, false);
        return false;
    }
    
    // Validate the draft before I/O. Saving is explicit; window state alone is not disk persistence.
    public static void apply(Window clicked) {
        String draft = clicked.widget("name").getText().trim();
        if (draft.equals("")) {
            clicked.getState().text("message", "Enter a name before saving.");
            return;
        }
        // This is deliberately a tiny local settings file. Large/network writes belong in a worker.
        // The API writes a temporary sibling before replacing the previous settings document.
        TextResult saved = OffscreenFiles.write("config/offscreen-settings.txt", draft);
        if (saved.success()) {
            clicked.getState()
                .text("message",
                "Saved. Close and reopen to load this value.");
        }
        else {
            clicked.getState().text("message", saved.error());
        }
    }
    
    // Reset affects the visible draft only. It must never silently overwrite the saved file.
    public static void reset(Window clicked) {
        clicked.widget("name").text("Player");
        clicked.getState()
            .text("message",
            "Default restored in the draft. Apply to save.");
    }
    
    // Discard the current draft by closing this exact owner; no write occurs.
    public static void cancel(Window clicked) {
        clicked.close();
    }
    
    // Close only this file's owned window. Closing also emits the screen close callback.
    // Call on the client thread; repeated calls are harmless. Never use global closeAll for addon cleanup.
    public static void close() {
        if (owned != null) {
            owned.close();
        }
        owned = null;
    }
    
}

    val screen as Screen = Windows.screen("Settings", 960, 640);
    val loaded as TextResult = Files.read("config/offscreen-settings.txt", "Player");
    screen.textField("name", 36, 105, 400, 24, loaded.value).maxLength(40);
    screen.defaults.text("message", "Edit the name, then apply your changes.");
    if (!loaded.success) {
        screen.defaults.text("message", loaded.error);
    }
    screen.button("Apply changes",
        36,
        158,
        120,
        26,
        function(clicked) {
        apply(clicked);
    })
        .flat()
        .shadow(false)
        .skin("normal",
        -15062988,
        -13614255,
        -1445387,
        1)
        .skin("hovered",
        -13612969,
        -10037571,
        -1445387,
        1);
    screen.button("Cancel",
        168,
        158,
        100,
        26,
        function(clicked) {
        cancel(clicked);
    })
        .flat()
        .shadow(false)
        .skin("normal",
        -15062988,
        -13614255,
        -1445387,
        1)
        .skin("hovered",
        -13612969,
        -10037571,
        -1445387,
        1);
    screen.button("Reset",
        280,
        158,
        100,
        26,
        function(clicked) {
        reset(clicked);
    })
        .flat()
        .shadow(false)
        .skin("normal",
        -15062988,
        -13614255,
        -1445387,
        1)
        .skin("hovered",
        -13612969,
        -10037571,
        -1445387,
        1);
    screen.on("draw", function(event) {
        return draw(event);
    });
    owned = screen.open();
}

// The widget renders its own editable field; this callback draws labels and validation feedback.
function draw(event as ScreenEvent) as bool {
    header(event);
    event.text("DISPLAY NAME", 36, 85, -6372673, false);
    event.text(event.state.text("message"), 24, 215, -1445387, false);
    return false;
}

// Validate the draft before I/O. Saving is explicit; window state alone is not disk persistence.
function apply(clicked as Window) as void {
    val draft as string = clicked.widget("name").text.trim();
    if (draft == "") {
        clicked.state.text("message", "Enter a name before saving.");
        return;
    }
    // This is deliberately a tiny local settings file. Large/network writes belong in a worker.
    // The API writes a temporary sibling before replacing the previous settings document.
    val saved as TextResult = Files.write("config/offscreen-settings.txt", draft);
    if (saved.success) {
        clicked.state.text("message", "Saved. Close and reopen to load this value.");
    }
    else {
        clicked.state.text("message", saved.error);
    }
}

// Reset affects the visible draft only. It must never silently overwrite the saved file.
function reset(clicked as Window) as void {
    clicked.widget("name").text("Player");
    clicked.state.text("message", "Default restored in the draft. Apply to save.");
}

// Discard the current draft by closing this exact owner; no write occurs.
function cancel(clicked as Window) as void {
    clicked.close();
}

// Close only this file's owned window. Closing also emits the screen close callback.
// Call on the client thread; repeated calls are harmless. Never use global closeAll for addon cleanup.
function close() as void {
    if (!isNull(owned)) {
        owned.close();
    }
    owned = null;
}

Searchable, scrollable list

Type into the search field, select a result and scroll through the remaining rows. Filtering retains the selected value, even if it is temporarily hidden. An empty result set displays a message instead of leaving stale rows visible.

package examples.single.java;

// Requires OffscreenCleanroom on Minecraft 1.12.2 Cleanroom.
// Add this file to your addon with its language runtime enabled.
// Call open() from a client key/button handler after joining a world; declarations open nothing.
// Call close() from your client-thread disconnect/unload hook.
// The server-action example additionally registers its panel during common startup on both sides.
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.script.OffscreenWindows;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.script.OffscreenWindows.*;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.script.OffscreenFiles;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.script.OffscreenFiles.*;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.script.OffscreenPanel;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.script.OffscreenPanel.Context;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.script.OffscreenPanel.Player;

public final class CatalogExample {
    // Retain the exact native handle. A title is not unique enough to prove ownership.
    private static Window owned = null;
    // Draw the same compact header at the current GUI size. Rendering stays on the client thread.
    public static void header(ScreenEvent event) {
        event.rect(0, 0, event.getWidth(), event.getHeight(), -15722464);
        event.rect(20, 20, 3, 16, -10103043);
        event.text("Material browser", 32, 23, -1445387, false);
        event.text("Search, scroll, and select a material.", 32, 42, -6372673, false);
        event.rect(20, 62, event.getWidth() - 40, 1, -13614255);
    }
    
    // Small local arithmetic helper; it is included rather than supplied by a hidden utility file.
    public static int minInt(int a, int b) {
        if (a < b) {
            return a;
        }
        return b;
    }
    
    // Clamp layout and scrolling without allocating objects during drawing.
    public static int maxInt(int a, int b) {
        if (a > b) {
            return a;
        }
        return b;
    }
    
    // The catalogue is immutable input. Filtering changes visibility, never the source list.
    private static String[] materials = new String[] {
        "Copper", "Silver", "Gold", "Tin", "Iron", "Nickel", "Cobalt", "Zinc", "Lead", "Platinum", "Iridium", "Osmium", "Titanium", "Aluminium", "Antimony", "Beryllium", "Bismuth", "Boron", "Cadmium", "Calcium", "Carbon", "Chromium", "Germanium", "Lithium", "Magnesium", "Manganese", "Molybdenum", "Niobium", "Palladium", "Potassium", "Silicon", "Sodium", "Tantalum", "Tellurium", "Tungsten", "Vanadium", "Zirconium"
    };
    // Count matching catalogue entries without retaining an ever-growing results history.
    public static int countMatches(String query) {
        int count = 0;
        String needle = query.toLowerCase(java.util.Locale.ROOT);
        for (int i = 0; i < materials.length; i++) {
            if (materials[i].toLowerCase(java.util.Locale.ROOT).contains(needle)) {
                count = count + 1;
            }
        }
        return count;
    }
    
    // Reserve the header and footer; only complete row slots are selectable.
    public static int rows(int height) {
        return maxInt(1, (height - 160) / 24);
    }
    
    // Build fresh screen state, declare callbacks, then open once. A returned handle can precede
    // the first layout; readiness is separate from ownership. No window opens during file loading.
    public static void open() {
        close();
        Screen screen = OffscreenWindows.screen("Material browser", 960, 640);
        screen.textField("search",
            28,
            78,
            420,
            24,
            "")
            .changed(widget -> searchChanged(widget));
        screen.getDefaults().integer("first", 0);
        screen.getDefaults().text("selection", "Choose a material");
        screen.on("draw", event -> draw(event));
        screen.on("click", event -> click(event));
        screen.on("scroll", event -> scroll(event));
        owned = screen.open();
    }
    
    // Restart scrolling after a query change. The selected identity is intentionally retained.
    public static void searchChanged(Widget widget) {
        widget.getState().integer("first", 0);
    }
    
    // Map filtered row indices into visible rectangles. Re-clamp after resize so the viewport never
    // starts beyond the end of a shorter result list. Selection is independent of filtering.
    public static boolean draw(ScreenEvent event) {
        header(event);
        String query = event.widget("search")
            .getText()
            .toLowerCase(java.util.Locale.ROOT);
        int first = maxInt(0,
            minInt(event.getState()
            .integer("first"),
            countMatches(query) - rows(event.getHeight())));
        event.getState().integer("first", first);
        int matched = 0;
        int visible = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < materials.length; i++) {
            String value = materials[i];
            if (value.toLowerCase(java.util.Locale.ROOT).contains(query)) {
                if (matched >= first && visible < rows(event.getHeight())) {
                    int top = 120 + visible * 24;
                    event.rect(20, top, 250, 22, -15062988);
                    if (value.equals(event.getState().text("selection"))) {
                        event.rect(20, top, 3, 22, -10103043);
                    }
                    event.text(value, 30, top + 7, -1445387, false);
                    visible = visible + 1;
                }
                matched = matched + 1;
            }
        }
        if (matched == 0) {
            event.text("No matching materials", 28, 130, -6372673, false);
        }
        event.text("SELECTION", 292, 125, -6372673, false);
        event.text(event.getState().text("selection"), 292, 153, -10103043, false);
        event.text("Results: " + matched, 24, event.getHeight() - 24, -6372673, false);
        return false;
    }
    
    // Invert the row layout to find the clicked filtered entry. Ignore clicks in the search field,
    // detail panel, footer and rows beyond the visible viewport.
    public static boolean click(ScreenEvent event) {
        if (event.getCode() != 0 || event.getX() < 20 || event.getX() >= 270 || event.getY() < 120) {
            return false;
        }
        int row = (event.getY() - 120) / 24;
        if (row >= rows(event.getHeight())) {
            return false;
        }
        int target = event.getState().integer("first") + row;
        int matched = 0;
        String query = event.widget("search")
            .getText()
            .toLowerCase(java.util.Locale.ROOT);
        for (int i = 0; i < materials.length; i++) {
            String value = materials[i];
            if (value.toLowerCase(java.util.Locale.ROOT).contains(query)) {
                if (matched == target) {
                    event.getState().text("selection", value);
                    return true;
                }
                matched = matched + 1;
            }
        }
        return false;
    }
    
    // Scroll a bounded number of rows. Drawing clamps the upper limit against the current query.
    public static boolean scroll(ScreenEvent event) {
        int step = 1;
        if (event.getCode() > 0) {
            step = -1;
        }
        event.getState()
            .integer("first",
            maxInt(0,
            event.getState()
            .integer("first") + step * 3));
        return true;
    }
    
    // Close only this file's owned window. Closing also emits the screen close callback.
    // Call on the client thread; repeated calls are harmless. Never use global closeAll for addon cleanup.
    public static void close() {
        if (owned != null) {
            owned.close();
        }
        owned = null;
    }
    
}

package examples.single.groovy

// Requires OffscreenCleanroom on Minecraft 1.12.2 Cleanroom.
// Add this file to your addon with its language runtime enabled.
// Call open() from a client key/button handler after joining a world; declarations open nothing.
// Call close() from your client-thread disconnect/unload hook.
// The server-action example additionally registers its panel during common startup on both sides.
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.script.OffscreenWindows as Windows
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.script.OffscreenFiles as Files
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.script.OffscreenPanel as Panel
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.script.OffscreenWindows.*
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.script.OffscreenFiles.*
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.script.OffscreenPanel.Context
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.script.OffscreenPanel.Player

@groovy.transform.CompileStatic
final class CatalogExample {
    // Retain the exact native handle. A title is not unique enough to prove ownership.
    private static Window owned = null;
    // Draw the same compact header at the current GUI size. Rendering stays on the client thread.
    public static void header(ScreenEvent event) {
        event.rect(0, 0, event.getWidth(), event.getHeight(), -15722464);
        event.rect(20, 20, 3, 16, -10103043);
        event.text("Material browser", 32, 23, -1445387, false);
        event.text("Search, scroll, and select a material.", 32, 42, -6372673, false);
        event.rect(20, 62, event.getWidth() - 40, 1, -13614255);
    }
    
    // Small local arithmetic helper; it is included rather than supplied by a hidden utility file.
    public static int minInt(double a, double b) {
        if (a < b) {
            return (int) (a);
        }
        return (int) (b);
    }
    
    // Clamp layout and scrolling without allocating objects during drawing.
    public static int maxInt(double a, double b) {
        if (a > b) {
            return (int) (a);
        }
        return (int) (b);
    }
    
    // The catalogue is immutable input. Filtering changes visibility, never the source list.
    private static String[] materials = ["Copper", "Silver", "Gold", "Tin", "Iron", "Nickel", "Cobalt", "Zinc", "Lead", "Platinum", "Iridium", "Osmium", "Titanium", "Aluminium", "Antimony", "Beryllium", "Bismuth", "Boron", "Cadmium", "Calcium", "Carbon", "Chromium", "Germanium", "Lithium", "Magnesium", "Manganese", "Molybdenum", "Niobium", "Palladium", "Potassium", "Silicon", "Sodium", "Tantalum", "Tellurium", "Tungsten", "Vanadium", "Zirconium"] as String[];
    // Count matching catalogue entries without retaining an ever-growing results history.
    public static int countMatches(String query) {
        int count = (int) (0);
        String needle = query.toLowerCase(java.util.Locale.ROOT);
        for (int i = 0; i < materials.length; i++) {
            if (materials[i].toLowerCase(java.util.Locale.ROOT).contains(needle)) {
                count = count + 1;
            }
        }
        return (int) (count);
    }
    
    // Reserve the header and footer; only complete row slots are selectable.
    public static int rows(int height) {
        return (int) (maxInt(1, (height - 160) / 24));
    }
    
    // Build fresh screen state, declare callbacks, then open once. A returned handle can precede
    // the first layout; readiness is separate from ownership. No window opens during file loading.
    public static void open() {
        close();
        Screen screen = Windows.screen("Material browser", 960, 640);
        screen.textField("search",
            28,
            78,
            420,
            24,
            "")
            .changed({
            Widget widget -> searchChanged(widget)
        });
        screen.getDefaults().integer("first", 0);
        screen.getDefaults().text("selection", "Choose a material");
        screen.on("draw", {
            ScreenEvent event -> draw(event)
        });
        screen.on("click", {
            ScreenEvent event -> click(event)
        });
        screen.on("scroll", {
            ScreenEvent event -> scroll(event)
        });
        owned = screen.open();
    }
    
    // Restart scrolling after a query change. The selected identity is intentionally retained.
    public static void searchChanged(Widget widget) {
        widget.getState().integer("first", 0);
    }
    
    // Map filtered row indices into visible rectangles. Re-clamp after resize so the viewport never
    // starts beyond the end of a shorter result list. Selection is independent of filtering.
    public static boolean draw(ScreenEvent event) {
        header(event);
        String query = event.widget("search")
            .getText()
            .toLowerCase(java.util.Locale.ROOT);
        int first = (int) (maxInt(0,
            minInt(event.getState()
            .integer("first"),
            countMatches(query) - rows(event.getHeight()))));
        event.getState().integer("first", first);
        int matched = (int) (0);
        int visible = (int) (0);
        for (int i = 0; i < materials.length; i++) {
            String value = materials[i];
            if (value.toLowerCase(java.util.Locale.ROOT).contains(query)) {
                if (matched >= first && visible < rows(event.getHeight())) {
                    int top = (int) (120 + visible * 24);
                    event.rect(20, top, 250, 22, -15062988);
                    if (value.equals(event.getState().text("selection"))) {
                        event.rect(20, top, 3, 22, -10103043);
                    }
                    event.text(value, 30, top + 7, -1445387, false);
                    visible = visible + 1;
                }
                matched = matched + 1;
            }
        }
        if (matched == 0) {
            event.text("No matching materials", 28, 130, -6372673, false);
        }
        event.text("SELECTION", 292, 125, -6372673, false);
        event.text(event.getState().text("selection"), 292, 153, -10103043, false);
        event.text("Results: " + matched, 24, event.getHeight() - 24, -6372673, false);
        return false;
    }
    
    // Invert the row layout to find the clicked filtered entry. Ignore clicks in the search field,
    // detail panel, footer and rows beyond the visible viewport.
    public static boolean click(ScreenEvent event) {
        if (event.getCode() != 0 || event.getX() < 20 || event.getX() >= 270 || event.getY() < 120) {
            return false;
        }
        int row = (int) ((event.getY() - 120) / 24);
        if (row >= rows(event.getHeight())) {
            return false;
        }
        int target = (int) (event.getState().integer("first") + row);
        int matched = (int) (0);
        String query = event.widget("search")
            .getText()
            .toLowerCase(java.util.Locale.ROOT);
        for (int i = 0; i < materials.length; i++) {
            String value = materials[i];
            if (value.toLowerCase(java.util.Locale.ROOT).contains(query)) {
                if (matched == target) {
                    event.getState().text("selection", value);
                    return true;
                }
                matched = matched + 1;
            }
        }
        return false;
    }
    
    // Scroll a bounded number of rows. Drawing clamps the upper limit against the current query.
    public static boolean scroll(ScreenEvent event) {
        int step = (int) (1);
        if (event.getCode() > 0) {
            step = -1;
        }
        event.getState()
            .integer("first",
            maxInt(0,
            event.getState()
            .integer("first") + step * 3));
        return true;
    }
    
    // Close only this file's owned window. Closing also emits the screen close callback.
    // Call on the client thread; repeated calls are harmless. Never use global closeAll for addon cleanup.
    public static void close() {
        if (owned != null) {
            owned.close();
        }
        owned = null;
    }
    
}

Live heap-usage graph

The graph samples used JVM heap every five client ticks and retains the newest 120 samples. Its vertical scale stays fixed at the JVM heap limit, so garbage collection does not resize earlier bars. The cards show used MiB, the heap limit and the retained sample count.

package examples.single.java;

// Requires OffscreenCleanroom on Minecraft 1.12.2 Cleanroom.
// Add this file to your addon with its language runtime enabled.
// Call open() from a client key/button handler after joining a world; declarations open nothing.
// Call close() from your client-thread disconnect/unload hook.
// The server-action example additionally registers its panel during common startup on both sides.
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.script.OffscreenWindows;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.script.OffscreenWindows.*;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.script.OffscreenFiles;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.script.OffscreenFiles.*;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.script.OffscreenPanel;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.script.OffscreenPanel.Context;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.script.OffscreenPanel.Player;

public final class MonitorExample {
    // Retain the exact native handle. A title is not unique enough to prove ownership.
    private static Window owned = null;
    // Draw the same compact header at the current GUI size. Rendering stays on the client thread.
    public static void header(ScreenEvent event) {
        event.rect(0, 0, event.getWidth(), event.getHeight(), -15722464);
        event.rect(20, 20, 3, 16, -10103043);
        event.text("Memory monitor", 32, 23, -1445387, false);
        event.text("Heap usage in MiB; 30 seconds of history.",
            32,
            42,
            -6372673,
            false);
        event.rect(20, 62, event.getWidth() - 40, 1, -13614255);
    }
    
    // Small local arithmetic helper; it is included rather than supplied by a hidden utility file.
    public static int minInt(int a, int b) {
        if (a < b) {
            return a;
        }
        return b;
    }
    
    // Clamp layout and scrolling without allocating objects during drawing.
    public static int maxInt(int a, int b) {
        if (a > b) {
            return a;
        }
        return b;
    }
    
    // Build fresh screen state, declare callbacks, then open once. A returned handle can precede
    // the first layout; readiness is separate from ownership. No window opens during file loading.
    public static void open() {
        close();
        Screen screen = OffscreenWindows.screen("Memory monitor", 960, 640);
        screen.getDefaults().integer("ticks", 0);
        screen.getDefaults().integer("cursor", 0);
        screen.getDefaults().integer("count", 0);
        screen.on("draw", event -> draw(event));
        screen.on("tick", event -> tick(event));
        owned = screen.open();
    }
    
    // Take one sample every five client ticks, independent of frame rate. Exactly 120 keys are reused
    // as a ring buffer; running for hours cannot grow the history or its memory footprint.
    public static boolean tick(ScreenEvent event) {
        int ticks = event.getState().integer("ticks") + 1;
        event.getState().integer("ticks", ticks);
        if (ticks % 5 != 0) {
            return false;
        }
        int cursor = event.getState().integer("cursor");
        event.getState().number("sample" + cursor, OffscreenWindows.usedHeapMiB());
        event.getState().integer("cursor", (cursor + 1) % 120);
        event.getState()
            .integer("count",
            minInt(120,
            event.getState()
            .integer("count") + 1));
        return false;
    }
    
    // Calculate columns from current GUI units, not desktop pixels. Cards retain their internal padding.
    // The chart reads oldest-to-newest even after wraparound; drawing never creates samples.
    public static boolean draw(ScreenEvent event) {
        header(event);
        int columns = 1;
        if (event.getWidth() >= 300) {
            columns = 2;
        }
        if (event.getWidth() >= 440) {
            columns = 3;
        }
        int cardWidth = maxInt(40,
            (event.getWidth() - 40 - (columns - 1) * 12) / columns);
        for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
            int left = 20 + (i % columns) * (cardWidth + 12);
            int top = 82 + (i / columns) * 76;
            event.rect(left, top, cardWidth, 64, -15062988);
            String label = "Used: -- MiB";
            if (event.getState().integer("count") > 0) {
                label = "Used: " + (int) (event.getState()
                    .number("sample" + ((event.getState()
                    .integer("cursor") + 119) % 120))) + " MiB";
            }
            if (i == 1) {
                label = "Limit: " + (int) (OffscreenWindows.heapLimitMiB()) + " MiB";
            }
            if (i == 2) {
                label = "Samples: " + event.getState().integer("count");
            }
            event.text(label, left + 12, top + 26, -1445387, false);
        }
        int top = 94 + ((3 + columns - 1) / columns) * 76;
        int bottom = event.getHeight() - 20;
        if (bottom - top < 25) {
            return false;
        }
        // Keep a fixed vertical scale for the entire session. Rescaling to the latest peak would
        // move every old bar whenever allocation or garbage collection changes that peak.
        int count = event.getState().integer("count");
        double peak = OffscreenWindows.heapLimitMiB();
        event.rect(20, top, event.getWidth() - 40, bottom - top, -15062988);
        for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
            int index = (event.getState().integer("cursor") - count + i + 120) % 120;
            int left = 20 + i * (event.getWidth() - 40) / 120;
            int height = (int) ((bottom - top - 4) * event.getState()
                .number("sample" + index) / peak);
            event.rect(left,
                bottom - height,
                maxInt(1,
                (event.getWidth() - 40) / 120),
                height,
                -10103043);
        }
        return false;
    }
    
    // Close only this file's owned window. Closing also emits the screen close callback.
    // Call on the client thread; repeated calls are harmless. Never use global closeAll for addon cleanup.
    public static void close() {
        if (owned != null) {
            owned.close();
        }
        owned = null;
    }
    
}

@groovy.transform.CompileStatic
final class MonitorExample {
    // Retain the exact native handle. A title is not unique enough to prove ownership.
    private static Window owned = null;
    // Draw the same compact header at the current GUI size. Rendering stays on the client thread.
    public static void header(ScreenEvent event) {
        event.rect(0, 0, event.getWidth(), event.getHeight(), -15722464);
        event.rect(20, 20, 3, 16, -10103043);
        event.text("Memory monitor", 32, 23, -1445387, false);
        event.text("Heap usage in MiB; 30 seconds of history.",
            32,
            42,
            -6372673,
            false);
        event.rect(20, 62, event.getWidth() - 40, 1, -13614255);
    }
    
    // Small local arithmetic helper; it is included rather than supplied by a hidden utility file.
    public static int minInt(double a, double b) {
        if (a < b) {
            return (int) (a);
        }
        return (int) (b);
    }
    
    // Clamp layout and scrolling without allocating objects during drawing.
    public static int maxInt(double a, double b) {
        if (a > b) {
            return (int) (a);
        }
        return (int) (b);
    }
    
    // Build fresh screen state, declare callbacks, then open once. A returned handle can precede
    // the first layout; readiness is separate from ownership. No window opens during file loading.
    public static void open() {
        close();
        Screen screen = Windows.screen("Memory monitor", 960, 640);
        screen.getDefaults().integer("ticks", 0);
        screen.getDefaults().integer("cursor", 0);
        screen.getDefaults().integer("count", 0);
        screen.on("draw", {
            ScreenEvent event -> draw(event)
        });
        screen.on("tick", {
            ScreenEvent event -> tick(event)
        });
        owned = screen.open();
    }
    
    // Take one sample every five client ticks, independent of frame rate. Exactly 120 keys are reused
    // as a ring buffer; running for hours cannot grow the history or its memory footprint.
    public static boolean tick(ScreenEvent event) {
        int ticks = (int) (event.getState().integer("ticks") + 1);
        event.getState().integer("ticks", ticks);
        if (ticks % 5 != 0) {
            return false;
        }
        int cursor = (int) (event.getState().integer("cursor"));
        event.getState().number("sample" + cursor, Windows.usedHeapMiB());
        event.getState().integer("cursor", (cursor + 1) % 120);
        event.getState()
            .integer("count",
            minInt(120,
            event.getState()
            .integer("count") + 1));
        return false;
    }
    
    // Calculate columns from current GUI units, not desktop pixels. Cards retain their internal padding.
    // The chart reads oldest-to-newest even after wraparound; drawing never creates samples.
    public static boolean draw(ScreenEvent event) {
        header(event);
        int columns = (int) (1);
        if (event.getWidth() >= 300) {
            columns = 2;
        }
        if (event.getWidth() >= 440) {
            columns = 3;
        }
        int cardWidth = (int) (maxInt(40,
            (event.getWidth() - 40 - (columns - 1) * 12) / columns));
        for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
            int left = (int) (20 + (i % columns) * (cardWidth + 12));
            int top = (int) (82 + i.intdiv(columns) * 76);
            event.rect(left, top, cardWidth, 64, -15062988);
            String label = "Used: -- MiB";
            if (event.getState().integer("count") > 0) {
                label = "Used: " + (int) (event.getState()
                    .number("sample" + ((event.getState()
                    .integer("cursor") + 119) % 120))) + " MiB";
            }
            if (i == 1) {
                label = "Limit: " + (int) (Windows.heapLimitMiB()) + " MiB";
            }
            if (i == 2) {
                label = "Samples: " + event.getState().integer("count");
            }
            event.text(label, left + 12, top + 26, -1445387, false);
        }
        int top = (int) (94 + (3 + columns - 1).intdiv(columns) * 76);
        int bottom = (int) (event.getHeight() - 20);
        if (bottom - top < 25) {
            return false;
        }
        // Keep a fixed vertical scale for the entire session. Rescaling to the latest peak would
        // move every old bar whenever allocation or garbage collection changes that peak.
        int count = (int) (event.getState().integer("count"));
        double peak = Windows.heapLimitMiB();
        event.rect(20, top, event.getWidth() - 40, bottom - top, -15062988);
        for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
            int index = (int) ((event.getState()
                .integer("cursor") - count + i + 120) % 120);
            int left = (int) (20 + i * (event.getWidth() - 40) / 120);
            int height = (int) ((int) ((bottom - top - 4) * event.getState()
                .number("sample" + index) / peak));
            event.rect(left,
                bottom - height,
                maxInt(1,
                (event.getWidth() - 40) / 120),
                height,
                -10103043);
        }
        return false;
    }
    
    // Close only this file's owned window. Closing also emits the screen close callback.
    // Call on the client thread; repeated calls are harmless. Never use global closeAll for addon cleanup.
    public static void close() {
        if (owned != null) {
            owned.close();
        }
        owned = null;
    }
    
}

Image viewer with zoom and pan

Use the wheel to zoom around the cursor, drag with the left button to pan, and choose Fit image to reset. The image is clipped to the viewport. The texture manager owns the packaged image; this screen restores the GL scissor state and does not delete a shared texture.

package examples.single.java;

// Requires OffscreenCleanroom on Minecraft 1.12.2 Cleanroom.
// Add this file to your addon with its language runtime enabled.
// Call open() from a client key/button handler after joining a world; declarations open nothing.
// Call close() from your client-thread disconnect/unload hook.
// The server-action example additionally registers its panel during common startup on both sides.
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.script.OffscreenWindows;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.script.OffscreenWindows.*;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.script.OffscreenFiles;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.script.OffscreenFiles.*;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.script.OffscreenPanel;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.script.OffscreenPanel.Context;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.script.OffscreenPanel.Player;

public final class ImageViewerExample {
    // Retain the exact native handle. A title is not unique enough to prove ownership.
    private static Window owned = null;
    // Draw the same compact header at the current GUI size. Rendering stays on the client thread.
    public static void header(ScreenEvent event) {
        event.rect(0, 0, event.getWidth(), event.getHeight(), -15722464);
        event.rect(20, 20, 3, 16, -10103043);
        event.text("Image viewer", 32, 23, -1445387, false);
        event.text("Scroll to zoom, drag to pan, or fit the image.",
            32,
            42,
            -6372673,
            false);
        event.rect(20, 62, event.getWidth() - 40, 1, -13614255);
    }
    
    // Small local arithmetic helper; it is included rather than supplied by a hidden utility file.
    public static int minInt(int a, int b) {
        if (a < b) {
            return a;
        }
        return b;
    }
    
    // Clamp layout and scrolling without allocating objects during drawing.
    public static int maxInt(int a, int b) {
        if (a > b) {
            return a;
        }
        return b;
    }
    
    // Build fresh screen state, declare callbacks, then open once. A returned handle can precede
    // the first layout; readiness is separate from ownership. No window opens during file loading.
    public static void open() {
        close();
        Screen screen = OffscreenWindows.screen("Image viewer", 960, 640);
        screen.getDefaults().number("zoom", 1.0);
        screen.getDefaults().number("left", 0.0);
        screen.getDefaults().number("top", 120.0);
        screen.getDefaults().integer("viewWidth", 480);
        screen.getDefaults().integer("viewHeight", 320);
        screen.button("Fit image",
            20,
            76,
            110,
            26,
            clicked -> fitButton(clicked))
            .flat()
            .shadow(false)
            .skin("normal",
            -15062988,
            -13614255,
            -1445387,
            1)
            .skin("hovered",
            -13612969,
            -10037571,
            -1445387,
            1);
        screen.on("draw", event -> draw(event));
        screen.on("resize", event -> resized(event));
        screen.on("scroll", event -> zoom(event));
        screen.on("click", event -> press(event));
        screen.on("drag", event -> drag(event));
        screen.on("release", event -> release(event));
        owned = screen.open();
    }
    
    // Use the smaller width/height ratio to preserve the 500x500 source aspect ratio. Center in the
    // viewport, not in the whole window, so the toolbar remains clear.
    public static void fit(State state) {
        double scale = (state.integer("viewWidth") - 40) / 500.0;
        double vertical = (state.integer("viewHeight") - 140) / 500.0;
        if (vertical < scale) {
            scale = vertical;
        }
        if (scale < 0.01) {
            scale = 0.01;
        }
        state.number("zoom", scale);
        state.number("left", (state.integer("viewWidth") - 500 * scale) / 2.0);
        state.number("top",
            120 + (state.integer("viewHeight") - 140 - 500 * scale) / 2.0);
    }
    
    // Fit reuses the most recent GUI dimensions retained by the resize callback.
    public static void fitButton(Window clicked) {
        fit(clicked.getState());
    }
    
    // Refit after resize so the image cannot remain stranded beyond the new viewport.
    public static boolean resized(ScreenEvent event) {
        event.getState().integer("viewWidth", event.getWidth());
        event.getState().integer("viewHeight", event.getHeight());
        fit(event.getState());
        return false;
    }
    
    // Clip only the image. The library restores the caller's scissor even when a drawing callback fails.
    public static boolean draw(ScreenEvent event) {
        header(event);
        event.clipped(20,
            120,
            maxInt(0,
            event.getWidth() - 40),
            maxInt(0,
            event.getHeight() - 140),
            canvas -> drawImage(canvas));
        return false;
    }
    
    // Draw a shared packaged texture. Change the resource identifier and source dimensions together.
    // Minecraft owns the texture; this example closes its window but never deletes the shared resource.
    public static boolean drawImage(ScreenEvent event) {
        int size = maxInt(1, (int) (500 * event.getState().number("zoom")));
        event.image("offscreencleanroom:logo.png",
            (int) (event.getState()
            .number("left")),
            (int) (event.getState()
            .number("top")),
            size,
            size);
        return false;
    }
    
    // Use the same viewport for drawing and hit testing; toolbar clicks must not begin a drag.
    public static boolean inside(ScreenEvent event) {
        return event.getX() >= 20 && event.getX() < event.getWidth() - 20 && event.getY() >= 120 && event.getY() < event.getHeight() - 20;
    }
    
    // Keep the same source pixel under the pointer by rescaling the pointer-to-image-origin distance.
    // Clamping magnification prevents division by zero and impractically large geometry.
    public static boolean zoom(ScreenEvent event) {
        if (!inside(event)) {
            return false;
        }
        double old = event.getState().number("zoom");
        double next = old / 1.2;
        if (event.getCode() > 0) {
            next = old * 1.2;
        }
        if (next < 0.01) {
            next = 0.01;
        }
        if (next > 16.0) {
            next = 16.0;
        }
        event.getState()
            .number("left",
            event.getX() - (event.getX() - event.getState()
            .number("left")) * next / old);
        event.getState()
            .number("top",
            event.getY() - (event.getY() - event.getState()
            .number("top")) * next / old);
        event.getState().number("zoom", next);
        return true;
    }
    
    // Only a left-button press inside the image owns the following drag.
    public static boolean press(ScreenEvent event) {
        if (event.getCode() != 0 || !inside(event)) {
            return false;
        }
        event.getState().flag("dragging", true);
        event.getState().integer("lastX", event.getX());
        event.getState().integer("lastY", event.getY());
        return true;
    }
    
    // Apply incremental movement, not the entire distance since mouse-down on every frame.
    public static boolean drag(ScreenEvent event) {
        if (!event.getState().flag("dragging")) {
            return false;
        }
        event.getState()
            .number("left",
            event.getState()
            .number("left") + event.getX() - event.getState()
            .integer("lastX"));
        event.getState()
            .number("top",
            event.getState()
            .number("top") + event.getY() - event.getState()
            .integer("lastY"));
        event.getState().integer("lastX", event.getX());
        event.getState().integer("lastY", event.getY());
        return true;
    }
    
    // Release drag ownership even when the pointer leaves the image viewport.
    public static boolean release(ScreenEvent event) {
        event.getState().flag("dragging", false);
        return false;
    }
    
    // Close only this file's owned window. Closing also emits the screen close callback.
    // Call on the client thread; repeated calls are harmless. Never use global closeAll for addon cleanup.
    public static void close() {
        if (owned != null) {
            owned.close();
        }
        owned = null;
    }
    
}

    // Keep the same source pixel under the pointer by rescaling the pointer-to-image-origin distance.
    // Clamping magnification prevents division by zero and impractically large geometry.
    fun zoom(event: ScreenEvent): Boolean {
        if (!inside(event)) {
            return false
        }
        val old: Double = event.getState().number("zoom")
        var next: Double = old / 1.2
        if (event.getCode() > 0) {
            next = old * 1.2
        }
        if (next < 0.01) {
            next = 0.01
        }
        if (next > 16.0) {
            next = 16.0
        }
        event.getState()
            .number("left",
            event.getX() - (event.getX() - event.getState()
            .number("left")) * next / old)
        event.getState()
            .number("top",
            event.getY() - (event.getY() - event.getState()
            .number("top")) * next / old)
        event.getState().number("zoom", next)
        return true
    }
    
    // Only a left-button press inside the image owns the following drag.
    fun press(event: ScreenEvent): Boolean {
        if (event.getCode() != 0 || !inside(event)) {
            return false
        }
        event.getState().flag("dragging", true)
        event.getState().integer("lastX", event.getX())
        event.getState().integer("lastY", event.getY())
        return true
    }
    
    // Apply incremental movement, not the entire distance since mouse-down on every frame.
    fun drag(event: ScreenEvent): Boolean {
        if (!event.getState().flag("dragging")) {
            return false
        }
        event.getState()
            .number("left",
            event.getState()
            .number("left") + event.getX() - event.getState()
            .integer("lastX"))
        event.getState()
            .number("top",
            event.getState()
            .number("top") + event.getY() - event.getState()
            .integer("lastY"))
        event.getState().integer("lastX", event.getX())
        event.getState().integer("lastY", event.getY())
        return true
    }
    
    // Release drag ownership even when the pointer leaves the image viewport.
    fun release(event: ScreenEvent): Boolean {
        event.getState().flag("dragging", false)
        return false
    }
    
    // Close only this file's owned window. Closing also emits the screen close callback.

    fun close(): Unit {
        if (owned != null) {
            owned!!.close()
        }
        owned = null
    }
    
}

        return false;
    }
    event.state.flag("dragging", true);
    event.state.integer("lastX", event.x);
    event.state.integer("lastY", event.y);
    return true;
}

// Apply incremental movement, not the entire distance since mouse-down on every frame.
function drag(event as ScreenEvent) as bool {
    if (!event.state.flag("dragging")) {
        return false;
    }
    event.state.number("left",
        event.state.number("left") + event.x - event.state.integer("lastX"));
    event.state.number("top",
        event.state.number("top") + event.y - event.state.integer("lastY"));
    event.state.integer("lastX", event.x);
    event.state.integer("lastY", event.y);
    return true;
}

// Release drag ownership even when the pointer leaves the image viewport.
function release(event as ScreenEvent) as bool {
    event.state.flag("dragging", false);
    return false;
}

// Close only this file's owned window. Closing also emits the screen close callback.
// Call on the client thread; repeated calls are harmless. Never use global closeAll for addon cleanup.
function close() as void {
    if (!isNull(owned)) {
        owned.close();
    }
    owned = null;
}

Background-loading file browser

Load up to 200 file names without blocking drawing. The library owns a bounded worker pool; this example owns one cancellable request. A client tick adopts the finished result. Reload cancels the old request, failures remain visible, and closing the window cancels unfinished work.

package examples.single.java;

// Requires OffscreenCleanroom on Minecraft 1.12.2 Cleanroom.
// Add this file to your addon with its language runtime enabled.
// Call open() from a client key/button handler after joining a world; declarations open nothing.
// Call close() from your client-thread disconnect/unload hook.
// The server-action example additionally registers its panel during common startup on both sides.
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.script.OffscreenWindows;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.script.OffscreenWindows.*;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.script.OffscreenFiles;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.script.OffscreenFiles.*;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.script.OffscreenPanel;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.script.OffscreenPanel.Context;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.script.OffscreenPanel.Player;

public final class FileBrowserExample {
    // Retain the exact native handle. A title is not unique enough to prove ownership.
    private static Window owned = null;
    // Draw the same compact header at the current GUI size. Rendering stays on the client thread.
    public static void header(ScreenEvent event) {
        event.rect(0, 0, event.getWidth(), event.getHeight(), -15722464);
        event.rect(20, 20, 3, 16, -10103043);
        event.text("File browser", 32, 23, -1445387, false);
        event.text("Background I/O; closing cancels the current request.",
            32,
            42,
            -6372673,
            false);
        event.rect(20, 62, event.getWidth() - 40, 1, -13614255);
    }
    
    // Small local arithmetic helper; it is included rather than supplied by a hidden utility file.
    public static int minInt(int a, int b) {
        if (a < b) {
            return a;
        }
        return b;
    }
    
    // Clamp layout and scrolling without allocating objects during drawing.
    public static int maxInt(int a, int b) {
        if (a > b) {
            return a;
        }
        return b;
    }
    
    // One request and one immutable result array belong to this file's single window.
    // The worker never calls these drawing functions or mutates GUI state.
    private static DirectoryTask pending = null;
    private static String[] names = new String[] {
    };
    // Build fresh screen state, declare callbacks, then open once. A returned handle can precede
    // the first layout; readiness is separate from ownership. No window opens during file loading.
    public static void open() {
        close();
        Screen screen = OffscreenWindows.screen("File browser", 960, 640);
        if (pending != null) {
            pending.close();
        }
        names = new String[] {
        };
        pending = OffscreenFiles.list("config", 200);
        screen.getDefaults().text("status", "Loading files...");
        screen.getDefaults().integer("first", 0);
        screen.button("Reload",
            364,
            76,
            96,
            26,
            clicked -> reload(clicked))
            .flat()
            .shadow(false)
            .skin("normal",
            -15062988,
            -13614255,
            -1445387,
            1)
            .skin("hovered",
            -13612969,
            -10037571,
            -1445387,
            1);
        screen.on("draw", event -> draw(event));
        screen.on("tick", event -> tick(event));
        screen.on("close", event -> disposed(event));
        screen.on("scroll", event -> scroll(event));
        owned = screen.open();
    }
    
    // Cancel the previous owner before submitting a replacement. A late old result cannot become current.
    public static void reload(Window clicked) {
        if (pending != null) {
            pending.close();
        }
        names = new String[] {
        };
        pending = OffscreenFiles.list("config", 200);
        clicked.getState().text("status", "Loading files...");
        clicked.getState().integer("first", 0);
    }
    
    // Poll without blocking. Adopt completed immutable data only during the client update callback,
    // then release the request. Errors are shown rather than mistaken for an empty directory.
    public static boolean tick(ScreenEvent event) {
        if (pending == null) {
            return false;
        }
        DirectoryTask task = pending;
        if (task.status().equals("running")) {
            return false;
        }
        if (task.status().equals("ready")) {
            names = task.entries();
            event.getState().text("status", "Files: " + names.length);
        }
        else {
            event.getState().text("status", task.error());
        }
        task.close();
        pending = null;
        return false;
    }
    
    // Render a bounded page of the adopted data. No directory reads occur in this callback.
    public static boolean draw(ScreenEvent event) {
        header(event);
        event.text(event.getState().text("status"), 24, 84, -1445387, false);
        int rows = maxInt(1, (event.getHeight() - 150) / 22);
        int first = maxInt(0,
            minInt(event.getState()
            .integer("first"),
            names.length - rows));
        event.getState().integer("first", first);
        for (int row = 0; row < rows; row++) {
            if (first + row < names.length) {
                event.rect(20, 115 + row * 22, event.getWidth() - 40, 21, -15062988);
                event.text(names[first + row], 30, 121 + row * 22, -1445387, false);
            }
        }
        event.text("Scroll to browse", 24, event.getHeight() - 20, -6372673, false);
        return false;
    }
    
    // Scroll only the viewport. The current immutable result is reused instead of reloading the directory.
    public static boolean scroll(ScreenEvent event) {
        int step = 3;
        if (event.getCode() > 0) {
            step = -3;
        }
        event.getState()
            .integer("first",
            maxInt(0,
            event.getState()
            .integer("first") + step));
        return true;

Two connected windows

The list and preview share one selection model, while the search query and scroll position stay in the list screen. Closing either window leaves its sibling usable. Calling open again restores only the missing window. Teardown closes both owned handles.

// Call open() from a client key/button handler after joining a world; declarations open nothing.
// Call close() from your client-thread disconnect/unload hook.
// The server-action example additionally registers its panel during common startup on both sides.
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.script.OffscreenWindows;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.script.OffscreenWindows.*;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.script.OffscreenFiles;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.script.OffscreenFiles.*;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.script.OffscreenPanel;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.script.OffscreenPanel.Context;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.script.OffscreenPanel.Player;

public final class ConnectedWindowsExample {
    // Retain the exact native handle. A title is not unique enough to prove ownership.
    private static Window owned = null;
    // Draw the same compact header at the current GUI size. Rendering stays on the client thread.
    public static void header(ScreenEvent event) {
        event.rect(0, 0, event.getWidth(), event.getHeight(), -15722464);
        event.rect(20, 20, 3, 16, -10103043);
        event.text("Material browser", 32, 23, -1445387, false);
        event.text("Search, scroll, and select a material.", 32, 42, -6372673, false);
        event.rect(20, 62, event.getWidth() - 40, 1, -13614255);
    }
    
    // Small local arithmetic helper; it is included rather than supplied by a hidden utility file.
    public static int minInt(int a, int b) {
        if (a < b) {
            return a;
        }
        return b;
    }
    
    // Clamp layout and scrolling without allocating objects during drawing.
    public static int maxInt(int a, int b) {
        if (a > b) {
            return a;
        }
        return b;
    }
    
    // The catalogue is immutable input. Filtering changes visibility, never the source list.
    private static String[] materials = new String[] {
        "Copper", "Silver", "Gold", "Tin", "Iron", "Nickel", "Cobalt", "Zinc", "Lead", "Platinum", "Iridium", "Osmium", "Titanium", "Aluminium", "Antimony", "Beryllium", "Bismuth", "Boron", "Cadmium", "Calcium", "Carbon", "Chromium", "Germanium", "Lithium", "Magnesium", "Manganese", "Molybdenum", "Niobium", "Palladium", "Potassium", "Silicon", "Sodium", "Tantalum", "Tellurium", "Tungsten", "Vanadium", "Zirconium"
    };
    // Both windows deliberately share this one value; query/scroll remain in the list window.
    private static String selection = "Choose a material";
    private static Window preview = null;
    // Count matching catalogue entries without retaining an ever-growing results history.
    public static int countMatches(String query) {
        int count = 0;
        String needle = query.toLowerCase(java.util.Locale.ROOT);
        for (int i = 0; i < materials.length; i++) {
            if (materials[i].toLowerCase(java.util.Locale.ROOT).contains(needle)) {
                count = count + 1;
            }
        }
        return count;
    }
    
    // Reserve the header and footer; only complete row slots are selectable.
    public static int rows(int height) {
        return maxInt(1, (height - 160) / 24);
    }
    
    // Open only missing windows. Closing either half leaves its sibling and shared selection usable.
    public static void open() {
        if (owned == null || !owned.isOpen()) {
            Screen screen = OffscreenWindows.screen("Materials", 960, 640);
            screen.textField("search",
                28,
                78,
                420,
                24,
                "")
                .changed(widget -> searchChanged(widget));
            screen.getDefaults().integer("first", 0);
            screen.getDefaults().text("selection", "Choose a material");
            screen.on("draw", event -> draw(event));
            screen.on("click", event -> click(event));
            screen.on("scroll", event -> scroll(event));
            owned = screen.open();
        }
        if (preview == null || !preview.isOpen()) {
            Screen details = OffscreenWindows.screen("Selection preview", 960, 640);
            details.on("draw", event -> drawPreview(event));
            preview = details.open();
        }
    }
    
    // Read the shared value on each draw rather than copying a stale selection when the preview opens.
    public static boolean drawPreview(ScreenEvent event) {
        event.rect(0, 0, event.getWidth(), event.getHeight(), -15722464);
        event.text("Selected material", 32, 36, -6372673, false);
        event.text(selection, 32, 84, -10103043, false);
        event.text("Selection is shared; search and scroll are independent.",
            32,
            132,
            -1445387,
            false);
        return false;
    }
    
    // Restart scrolling after a query change. The selected identity is intentionally retained.
    public static void searchChanged(Widget widget) {
        widget.getState().integer("first", 0);
    }
    
    // Map filtered row indices into visible rectangles. Re-clamp after resize so the viewport never
    // starts beyond the end of a shorter result list. Selection is independent of filtering.
    public static boolean draw(ScreenEvent event) {
        header(event);
        String query = event.widget("search")
            .getText()
            .toLowerCase(java.util.Locale.ROOT);
        int first = maxInt(0,
            minInt(event.getState()
            .integer("first"),
            countMatches(query) - rows(event.getHeight())));
        event.getState().integer("first", first);
        int matched = 0;
        int visible = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < materials.length; i++) {
            String value = materials[i];
            if (value.toLowerCase(java.util.Locale.ROOT).contains(query)) {
                if (matched >= first && visible < rows(event.getHeight())) {
                    int top = 120 + visible * 24;
                    event.rect(20, top, 250, 22, -15062988);
                    if (value.equals(selection)) {
                        event.rect(20, top, 3, 22, -10103043);
                    }
                    event.text(value, 30, top + 7, -1445387, false);
                    visible = visible + 1;
                }
                matched = matched + 1;
            }
        }
        if (matched == 0) {
            event.text("No matching materials", 28, 130, -6372673, false);
        }
        event.text("SELECTION", 292, 125, -6372673, false);
        event.text(selection, 292, 153, -10103043, false);
        event.text("Results: " + matched, 24, event.getHeight() - 24, -6372673, false);
        return false;
    }
    
    // Invert the row layout to find the clicked filtered entry. Ignore clicks in the search field,
    // detail panel, footer and rows beyond the visible viewport.
    public static boolean click(ScreenEvent event) {
        if (event.getCode() != 0 || event.getX() < 20 || event.getX() >= 270 || event.getY() < 120) {
            return false;
        }
        int row = (event.getY() - 120) / 24;
        if (row >= rows(event.getHeight())) {
            return false;
        }
        int target = event.getState().integer("first") + row;
        int matched = 0;
        String query = event.widget("search")
            .getText()
            .toLowerCase(java.util.Locale.ROOT);
        for (int i = 0; i < materials.length; i++) {
            String value = materials[i];
            if (value.toLowerCase(java.util.Locale.ROOT).contains(query)) {
                if (matched == target) {
                    selection = value;
                    return true;
                }
                matched = matched + 1;
            }
        }
        return false;
    }
    
    // Scroll a bounded number of rows. Drawing clamps the upper limit against the current query.
    public static boolean scroll(ScreenEvent event) {
        int step = 1;
        if (event.getCode() > 0) {
            step = -1;
        }
        event.getState()
            .integer("first",
            maxInt(0,
            event.getState()
            .integer("first") + step * 3));
        return true;
    }
    
    // Close only this file's owned window. Closing also emits the screen close callback.
    // Call on the client thread; repeated calls are harmless. Never use global closeAll for addon cleanup.
    public static void close() {
        if (preview != null) {
            preview.close();
        }
        preview = null;
        if (owned != null) {
            owned.close();
        }
        owned = null;
    }
    
}

@groovy.transform.CompileStatic
final class ConnectedWindowsExample {
    // Retain the exact native handle. A title is not unique enough to prove ownership.
    private static Window owned = null;
    // Draw the same compact header at the current GUI size. Rendering stays on the client thread.
    public static void header(ScreenEvent event) {
        event.rect(0, 0, event.getWidth(), event.getHeight(), -15722464);
        event.rect(20, 20, 3, 16, -10103043);
        event.text("Material browser", 32, 23, -1445387, false);
        event.text("Search, scroll, and select a material.", 32, 42, -6372673, false);
        event.rect(20, 62, event.getWidth() - 40, 1, -13614255);
    }
    
    // Small local arithmetic helper; it is included rather than supplied by a hidden utility file.
    public static int minInt(double a, double b) {
        if (a < b) {
            return (int) (a);
        }
        return (int) (b);
    }
    
    // Clamp layout and scrolling without allocating objects during drawing.
    public static int maxInt(double a, double b) {
        if (a > b) {
            return (int) (a);
        }
        return (int) (b);
    }
    
    // The catalogue is immutable input. Filtering changes visibility, never the source list.
    private static String[] materials = ["Copper", "Silver", "Gold", "Tin", "Iron", "Nickel", "Cobalt", "Zinc", "Lead", "Platinum", "Iridium", "Osmium", "Titanium", "Aluminium", "Antimony", "Beryllium", "Bismuth", "Boron", "Cadmium", "Calcium", "Carbon", "Chromium", "Germanium", "Lithium", "Magnesium", "Manganese", "Molybdenum", "Niobium", "Palladium", "Potassium", "Silicon", "Sodium", "Tantalum", "Tellurium", "Tungsten", "Vanadium", "Zirconium"] as String[];
    // Both windows deliberately share this one value; query/scroll remain in the list window.
    private static String selection = "Choose a material";
    private static Window preview = null;
    // Count matching catalogue entries without retaining an ever-growing results history.
    public static int countMatches(String query) {
        int count = (int) (0);
        String needle = query.toLowerCase(java.util.Locale.ROOT);
        for (int i = 0; i < materials.length; i++) {
            if (materials[i].toLowerCase(java.util.Locale.ROOT).contains(needle)) {
                count = count + 1;
            }
        }
        return (int) (count);
    }
    
    // Reserve the header and footer; only complete row slots are selectable.
    public static int rows(int height) {
        return (int) (maxInt(1, (height - 160) / 24));
    }
    
    // Open only missing windows. Closing either half leaves its sibling and shared selection usable.
    public static void open() {
        if (owned == null || !owned.isOpen()) {
            Screen screen = Windows.screen("Materials", 960, 640);
            screen.textField("search",
                28,
                78,
                420,
                24,
                "")
                .changed({
                Widget widget -> searchChanged(widget)
            });
            screen.getDefaults().integer("first", 0);
            screen.getDefaults().text("selection", "Choose a material");
            screen.on("draw", {
                ScreenEvent event -> draw(event)
            });
            screen.on("click", {
                ScreenEvent event -> click(event)
            });
            screen.on("scroll", {
                ScreenEvent event -> scroll(event)
            });
            owned = screen.open();
        }
        if (preview == null || !preview.isOpen()) {
            Screen details = Windows.screen("Selection preview", 960, 640);
            details.on("draw", {
                ScreenEvent event -> drawPreview(event)
            });
            preview = details.open();
        }
    }
    
    // Read the shared value on each draw rather than copying a stale selection when the preview opens.
    public static boolean drawPreview(ScreenEvent event) {
        event.rect(0, 0, event.getWidth(), event.getHeight(), -15722464);
        event.text("Selected material", 32, 36, -6372673, false);
        event.text(selection, 32, 84, -10103043, false);
        event.text("Selection is shared; search and scroll are independent.",
            32,
            132,
            -1445387,
            false);
        return false;
    }
    
    // Restart scrolling after a query change. The selected identity is intentionally retained.
    public static void searchChanged(Widget widget) {
        widget.getState().integer("first", 0);
    }
    
    // Map filtered row indices into visible rectangles. Re-clamp after resize so the viewport never
    // starts beyond the end of a shorter result list. Selection is independent of filtering.
    public static boolean draw(ScreenEvent event) {
        header(event);
        String query = event.widget("search")
            .getText()
            .toLowerCase(java.util.Locale.ROOT);
        int first = (int) (maxInt(0,
            minInt(event.getState()
            .integer("first"),
            countMatches(query) - rows(event.getHeight()))));
        event.getState().integer("first", first);
        int matched = (int) (0);
        int visible = (int) (0);
        for (int i = 0; i < materials.length; i++) {
            String value = materials[i];
            if (value.toLowerCase(java.util.Locale.ROOT).contains(query)) {
                if (matched >= first && visible < rows(event.getHeight())) {
                    int top = (int) (120 + visible * 24);
                    event.rect(20, top, 250, 22, -15062988);
                    if (value.equals(selection)) {
                        event.rect(20, top, 3, 22, -10103043);
                    }
                    event.text(value, 30, top + 7, -1445387, false);
                    visible = visible + 1;
                }
                matched = matched + 1;
            }
        }
        if (matched == 0) {
            event.text("No matching materials", 28, 130, -6372673, false);
        }
        event.text("SELECTION", 292, 125, -6372673, false);
        event.text(selection, 292, 153, -10103043, false);
        event.text("Results: " + matched, 24, event.getHeight() - 24, -6372673, false);
        return false;
    }
    
    // Invert the row layout to find the clicked filtered entry. Ignore clicks in the search field,
    // detail panel, footer and rows beyond the visible viewport.
    public static boolean click(ScreenEvent event) {
        if (event.getCode() != 0 || event.getX() < 20 || event.getX() >= 270 || event.getY() < 120) {
            return false;
        }
        int row = (int) ((event.getY() - 120) / 24);
        if (row >= rows(event.getHeight())) {
            return false;
        }
        int target = (int) (event.getState().integer("first") + row);
        int matched = (int) (0);
        String query = event.widget("search")
            .getText()
            .toLowerCase(java.util.Locale.ROOT);
        for (int i = 0; i < materials.length; i++) {
            String value = materials[i];
            if (value.toLowerCase(java.util.Locale.ROOT).contains(query)) {
                if (matched == target) {
                    selection = value;
                    return true;
                }
                matched = matched + 1;
            }
        }
        return false;
    }
    
    // Scroll a bounded number of rows. Drawing clamps the upper limit against the current query.
    public static boolean scroll(ScreenEvent event) {
        int step = (int) (1);
        if (event.getCode() > 0) {
            step = -1;
        }
        event.getState()
            .integer("first",
            maxInt(0,
            event.getState()
            .integer("first") + step * 3));
        return true;
    }
    
    // Close only this file's owned window. Closing also emits the screen close callback.
    // Call on the client thread; repeated calls are harmless. Never use global closeAll for addon cleanup.
    public static void close() {
        if (preview != null) {
            preview.close();
        }
        preview = null;
        if (owned != null) {
            owned.close();
        }
        owned = null;
    }
    
}

        return false;

        step = -1;

    owned = null;
